changes: Retains six sampler Machines, Recorder, explicit FORMAT SAMPLES setup and 42-channel USB audio (USB audio untested on R027).

R023 adds SEM as a seventh filter: Faust's Oberheim state-variable model (vaeffects.lib `oberheim`, Eric Tarr, STK-4.3). TYPE 0 low-pass, 63 notch, 126 high-pass, 127 band-pass, with smooth blends between. FREQ, RESO (Q 0.5–10), filter envelope, keytracking and modulation drive it; every voice keeps independent left/right state.

R024 keeps SEM's equations but runs its block loop from SHARC registers with a hardware loop and saves 34 instead of 99 registers per call (settled 32-sample loop: 5,390 → 1,755 emulated instructions).

R025 runs the relocated right effects chain only for sampler voices. The emulator attributes the R023/R024 overload to that duplicated chain and predicts about 81.7% of the DSP block with SEM on 16 slots (R024: 100.3%); the model excludes interrupts, cache, DMA and USB. Left-lane audio and sampler right-lane audio are unchanged, except that R024's one block of leftover right-channel audio after a sampler takes over an FM slot is gone.
R026 draws SEM's computed response on the FILTER page (log magnitude from FREQ, RESO and TYPE), replacing R023's schematic.
R027 shows LP · NOTCH · HP on the SEM TYPE widget for TYPE 0–126 and the band-pass icon alone at 127. Other filters keep the stock widget.
Sound-lock-aware sample usage and restoration references; per-Machine held-trig edits; rejected slice splits preserve markers.
Native sampler SYN copy/paste/clear/undo/randomize and FUNC controls; held-trig sample bank display; occupied-slot sample selection.
Stricter sample header/read validation and staged replacement preserve resident audio on rejected replacements; Recorder assignment failures preserve the original Sound.
SLICE note/span and reverse-loop bounds; held voices retire safely when a replacement sample becomes shorter; short-sample STRETCH grain offsets remain within the asset.
All six samplers use CC 40–47 and NRPN 1:73–80 for SYN controls. SAMP CC43 selects within the current bank; NRPN1:76 selects absolute positions 0–1023.
Bounds and failure handling for kit SysEx, song row counts, Euclidean rests and final timed outbound MIDI note release.

SLICE grids survive native same-device Sound/project save and reload via content-addressed companion files. Save failures propagate; failed new writes can retry; deferred restoration covers active tracks and preset-pool Sounds.

R020 fixes the R019 cold-start readiness defect: slice companion allocation/I/O waits for initialized filesystem startup status and mounted flag. DSP, USB ownership checks and control-frame ordering are unchanged from R019.
R021 reconciles the exposed SYN page after switching between stock synth and sampler Machines, restoring the SAMP knob popup through native view ownership and selection.
R022 includes sample identities in incremental working-project settings snapshots. Normal reboot recovery no longer depends on an explicit SAVE PROJECT to refresh this companion table.

The autosave hook reuses the project lock, checks current ownership and project identity, preserves explicit saved snapshots, and skips sample copy/CRC when unchanged. Recorder preferences sharing the companion header are refreshed separately.

Independent pre-publication review (2026-11-11): no private data; no vendor tables or graphics in published bytes; every recipe byte accounted for. Its wording, licence-notice and input-validation fixes are applied.

validation.notes: R027 is an owner-tested candidate (owner reports, not instrumented). R012 remains stable. R023 and R024 failed on hardware (DSP overload) and are not published.

source_reproduction.notes: The browser recipe reproduces the exact R027 MAIN, DSP and SysEx from the two official OS files. Current R023–R027 DSP sources rebuild the shipped kernel and R024/R025 DSP byte for byte. `build.py` still stops at R022; R023–R027 sources are in port/sem-filter.

known_issues: USB audio is untested on R027. It was reported broken on R023/R024 during their DSP overload. If you depend on USB audio, keep R012 until it is confirmed.
SEM costs more DSP time than the stock filters. R025's gate keeps the predicted worst case at 81.7% of the block; heavy use alongside many sampler voices is not yet measured on hardware.
The SEM TYPE widget appears only on the FILTER page; anywhere else the stock TYPE icons are shown.
Transfer can stop on the stock 'SUCCESS! REBOOTING' screen after installing (seen with R026). Switch the DN2 off and on; it then boots the new OS.

Native Sound/project exports carry slice-grid keys, not the companion files. They are incomplete backups of slice edits; cross-device restore or formatting requires the companion files. Automatic bundling/restoration is not implemented.
Intermittent internal audio-track hung notes remain unresolved; the outbound MIDI expiry fix is a separate path.
Bulk sample uploads/restoration can interrupt playback. Stop playback during transfers and wait until they finish; report problems that persist afterward.
A DSP transfer timeout can require restart even when the host retains the original sample binding.
Emulator instruction/model limits and filesystem/scheduler fixtures prevent treating offline results as complete hardware or manual compliance.
An iPhone USB freeze was reported; its cause remains unconfirmed. R022 is not a USB-freeze fix.
Abrupt power loss or a frozen task may prevent queued backup work from finishing. Sample companion writes are not atomic crash recovery; already-lost assignments cannot be reconstructed by this fix.
The targeted first-D popup routing defect is fixed in native replay; broader physical UI timing remains unverified.

sem_filter.model: Faust vaeffects.lib oberheim (Eric Tarr), STK-4.3 licence; a SEM-family state-variable model, not a measurement of a particular instrument
sem_filter.controls: FREQ, RESO, TYPE, filter envelope, keytracking and modulation
sem_filter.display: FILTER page response curve (R026) and LP / NOTCH / HP TYPE widget, band-pass alone at 127 (R027)
